title: What If You Always Brushed Right After Eating?

scenes.text: What if you brushed your teeth the second you finished eating? It can wear them down faster.
After a meal, your mouth turns acidic. It takes thirty to sixty minutes to recover.
Acidic food and drinks soften the outer layer of enamel for a while.
In one study, volunteers wore enamel samples in their mouths for 21 days, dipped in soda and brushed.
Brushed right away, they lost about six point eight microns. After an hour's wait, about four point eight.
Saliva rebuilds the enamel while you wait. So after anything acidic, give it an hour.

description:
What if you always brushed right after eating? Acidic food and drink temporarily soften enamel, and mouth pH takes about 30 to 60 minutes to recover.
In a 2001 in-situ study, enamel brushed immediately after a soft-drink attack lost about 6.8 microns versus about 4.8 microns after a 60-minute wait. The ADA and Oral Health Foundation suggest waiting up to an hour after acidic foods.
